name: Week 20 KB Saturday Cardio — Conditioning (Spotlight: Snatch; Clean-Squat-Press Triplet Finisher)
description: Saturday KB OPTION — pure conditioning, distinct from Tue (figure-8 flow + bottoms-up clean) and Thu (lighter skill template). **Warmup reminder:** halo → easy two-handed swings → goblet squat → internal core fist rotation → bottoms-up press (18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane), then the abbreviated 4-move banded prep. Light bell throughout (16-20lb) — breathing rate and sustainability are the targets, not load. Deliberately compact so it stays a clean skip when the week's been heavy: the Asgooch cardio complex carries over, then the finisher rotates this week to a clean-squat-press triplet. Spotlight rotates to the snatch — the explosive punch-through catch. Optional light push-press ladder if you want a strength touch. Choice-of-the-day on D6 alongside stairmaster, easy run, or rest.

dayOverview.theme: Saturday conditioning — light bell, breathing-rate target. Kept compact: Asgooch cardio complex + a clean-squat-press triplet finisher — so it's a clean skip on a heavy week. Day after Friday legs — squatting stays LIGHT on purpose. Spotlight rotates to the snatch. Optional light push-press ladder available.

spotlights.why: Rotates in as this week's spotlight (W19 was the high pull — the natural next rung up: high pull → snatch). The snatch is the full hip-driven punch-through: the hips float the bell, the hand punches THROUGH at the top for a soft overhead catch (no bang). Spotlight drills the punch-through timing + the soft catch so the power comes from the hips, not the shoulder. Right-shoulder-friendly when the hip does the work — sub the high pull if the catch crackles.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Finisher rotates: W18 high-rep ladder · W19 round-the-clock chain · W20 clean-squat-press triplet (current) · W21 cycle forward — a fresh complex. Spotlight rotates: W18 swing clean · W19 high pull · W20 snatch · W21 front squat or a fresh pick. The Asgooch cardio complex stays; the finisher + spotlight rotate so Saturday stays fresh.
watchpoints: **Saturday is optional and deliberately compact** — keep it a clean skip when the week's been heavy. The point is to not over-train into a weak Monday; weekends stay light.
**Day after Friday legs.** Squatting (front squat × 6 in the complex; the finisher front squat) stays LIGHT — 16-20lb. Skip the squat reps if the QL/quads are talking.
**Light bell is the whole point** — 16-20lb working. Conditioning means breathing rate, not bell weight.

**Snatch spotlight (inside the Asgooch complex)** — hips float the bell, punch the hand THROUGH at the top for a soft catch, no bang. The hip does the work, not the arm/shoulder. Right shoulder watch — sub high pulls if it crackles on the catch.
**Finisher rotated to a clean-squat-press triplet** — swing clean → front squat → push press, one continuous flow each side, 3-4 rounds. Light bell, keep moving.

**OPTIONAL light push-press ladder** — you ran 40/45/50 × 8/7/6 here W17 and it 'worked great.' If you want a strength touch, run it after the warm-up (clean to rack, dip-drive, pack the shoulder down). Keep it light and optional — Saturday's still a conditioning day.
**Choice-of-the-day on D6** — not mandatory. Skip if Friday legs cooked you; swap for stairmaster / easy run if cardio-only is the call. No pull-up greasing here — Saturday is the conditioning flank.

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Loosen the shoulders fast — the cardio complex is its own warmup.
Easy two-handed swings. Prime the hinge.
Light, open the hips. Skip if Friday legs left the quads sore.
Standing, torso hinged slightly forward. Wakes the grip + forearm + posterior chain — primes the clean catch + the snatch punch-through.

**LOAD:** 18lb. Your bottoms-up shoulder warmup — bell inverted/balanced over a vertical forearm, hard grip, shoulder packed. **8/side in two planes:** forward press + T-press. **Keep the T-plane lighter.** Fires the rotator cuff and primes the right shoulder before the overhead work.

sets.name: 🔆 Asgooch Cardio Complex — LEFT (Snatch Spotlight)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Left hand. Hips back, back flat, pull the elbow past the ribs. 2s pull, 2s lower.
Left hand. Hip drive into the rack — the hinge throws the bell up, the arm guides it; soft catch, knees absorb, elbow tucks to the ribs, no forearm bang. Ribs down at the rack.
Left rack. **LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Sit tall, full depth IF the legs are fresh; reduce depth before load if they're cooked.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the punch-through catch:**
- **Hips float the bell** — the hinge-and-snap throws it up; the arm just guides
- **Punch the hand THROUGH at the top** — the bell rotates around the wrist into a soft overhead catch, no bang on the forearm
- **Controlled lower** back into the hinge — re-load the hips
- **Right shoulder watch** — sub high pulls for the last 2 rounds if it crackles on the catch. Hip-driven is the shoulder-safe version.

Reflection: does the bell float up on the hip snap with a soft punch-through catch, or does the arm start muscling it up once you tire? Hip-driven = the win.

sets.notes: 5 rounds LEFT. Continuous within a round — row → clean → squat → snatch with no rest. Rest 30-45s between rounds. **Weak side first.** The snatch is the spotlight — drill the punch-through.

sets.name: 🔆 Asgooch Cardio Complex — RIGHT (Snatch Spotlight)

exercises.notes: Right hand. Same form — hips back, full extension.
Right hand. Hip drive, soft knees-absorb catch, no forearm bang.
Right rack. Same depth/load discipline as the left.
**🔆 SPOTLIGHT** — right hand. Punch the hand THROUGH for a soft catch; hips do the work. Right shoulder watch on the catch — same modify-to-high-pull rule.

sets.notes: 5 rounds RIGHT. Continuous within a round. **If the workout is running long after the left side, drop to 3-4 rounds right — don't grind a quality session into a sloppy one.**

sets.name: 🕐 Clean-Squat-Press Triplet (Rotated In for W20)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Hip drive into the rack, soft knees-absorb catch, no forearm bang. Ribs down at the rack — opens the triplet.
From the rack — full depth, chest up. **LIGHT**, Friday legs is yesterday. Skip or halve if the quads are tight.
Light dip-drive — the legs power the press, pack the shoulder DOWN on the lockout. **Right shoulder watch** — keep it light; lighten or skip if the overhead gets ugly.

sets.notes: **Clean-squat-press triplet — one continuous flow through the three moves each side, 4 rounds.** Single light bell (16-20lb). Clean → front squat → push press with minimal rest, ~30-45s between rounds. Posture + breathing-rate focus, not max effort. Drop to 3 rounds if the session's running long. (Rotated in from W19's round-the-clock chain.)

tips: **Saturday conditioning option — choice-of-the-day on D6.** Alternates with stairmaster, easy run, or rest. Skip if Friday legs cooked you; deliberately compact so skipping it costs nothing.
**LIGHT bell throughout: 16-20lb working.** This is the whole point. Conditioning = breathing rate, not load.
**Core block carries over:** the Asgooch CARDIO complex (row/clean/squat/snatch × 6 × 5 rounds per side).
**Snatch spotlight (inside the complex)** — hips float the bell, punch the hand THROUGH for a soft catch, no bang. The hip does the work, not the shoulder.
**Finisher rotated to a clean-squat-press triplet** — swing clean → front squat → push press, one continuous flow each side, 4 rounds, light bell.

**OPTIONAL light push-press ladder** — you ran 40/45/50 × 8/7/6 here W17 and it 'worked great.' Add it after the warm-up if you want a strength touch; keep it light, run the full banded prep if you do.
**Squatting stays LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Skip the squat reps if the quads are tight.
**Right shoulder watch on the snatch / clean / push press** — light bell, hip-driven; switch to plain swings / high pulls if it crackles.
**Bottoms-up press standard in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane (T-plane light).
**No pull-up greasing here** — Saturday is the conditioning flank.
Rotation plan: W21 rotates the finisher to a fresh complex + the spotlight to the front squat or a fresh pick.
formPhilosophy: Saturday is conditioning, distinct from the Tue and Thu KB days. Light bell, more reps. Kept deliberately compact — the Asgooch complex plus a rotating finisher (this week a clean-squat-press triplet) — so it's a genuine choice, not an obligation: easy to skip on a heavy week, and light enough it never bleeds into a weak Monday. The snatch spotlight drills the hip-driven, shoulder-safe punch-through, the natural next rung from last week's high pull. The optional push-press ladder stays optional so Saturday's identity as the light conditioning flank holds. Building decades, not weeks.
